page: Vultr vbm-4c-32gb is a dedicated bare-metal server in the Bare Metal SSD line. The machine runs on a four-core, eight-thread Intel Xeon 1270 processor clocked at 3.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning stands at 32 GB of system RAM, allocating 4.0 GB per virtual processing thread. Local storage is provided via an integrated 480 GB solid-state drive, and the server includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address without hardware GPU acceleration.

Hardware instruction extensions cover baseline vector and crypto routines including AVX, AES, and FMA, while newer AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets are absent. In benchmark testing, the platform produces mid-tier integer and general processing metrics, scoring 1509.0 in Geekbench single-core and 5137.0 in multi-core evaluation. While PassMark memory testing registers in the upper 10 percent at 3192.31 points, large uncached memory block throughput drops to 31.11 GB/sec for reads and 14.73 GB/sec for writes. Computational workloads such as PassMark physics score in the lower quartile at 717.17.

Eliminating hypervisor overhead yields steady operational throughput for standard data workflows. The server executes 8.08 million Redis SET operations per second and handles 7.05 GB/sec of static web throughput. However, lacking AVX-512 and accelerated matrix operations, inference with medium-scale 7B language models remains low at 16.42 prompt tokens per second and 6.87 generation tokens per second.

The absence of virtualization contention paired with direct SSD access offers solid utility for edge deployments, dedicated application hosting, continuous integration runners, caching layers, and relational or key-value databases that fit within 32 GB of memory.
description: Vultr vbm-4c-32gb is a bare-metal server providing dedicated access to a four-core, eight-thread Intel Xeon 1270 processor running at 3.8 GHz. Equipped with 32 GB of system memory, an onboard 480 GB SSD, and no GPU hardware, it delivers unvirtualized hardware execution on the x86_64 architecture. Benchmark metrics show reliable mid-tier compute capabilities, recording 1509.0 in single-core Geekbench and 8.08 million Redis SET operations per second. PassMark memory testing ranks in the top ten percent, although sustained uncached read and write bandwidths are constrained to 31.11 GB/sec and 14.73 GB/sec. Due to the lack of modern AVX-512 and matrix extensions, large-model machine learning throughput is limited. The system is well configured for dedicated web serving, caching tiers, intermediate relational databases, build agents, and single-tenant backend services requiring consistent hardware isolation.
